subject: AcmeHealth \u0014 Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>, Ben Morales <ben.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: AcmeHealth - Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up

Hi Alice / Ben,

Thanks again for the time this morning  appreciated the deep dive on your use case and the compliance constraints. As promised, a short recap + next steps so we can align internally and get a tailored deployment plan over to you.

Recap from today's call:
- Workload: LLM-based clinical triage assistant for patient intake (text input only).
- Data types: patient identifiers (name, dob, mrn), clinical notes (PHI), and some anonymized metadata. You confirmed PHI will be in scope.
- Desired deployment: Private VPC or on-prem (air-gapped) option to prevent any egress outside your VPC/colo.
- Key controls required: no egress of raw inputs/outputs, KMS-managed keys with customer control, audit logs retained per AcmeHealth policy, and support for SSO (SAML/OIDC).

Open questions we flagged for you to confirm:
1) Retention: you mentioned default retention is 7 years for clinical records  is that the retention requirement for logs/audit events as well?
2) Residency: do any of your sites require strictly on-prem (no cloud regions) or is a VPC in our US region acceptable provided egress is blocked?
3) Access: which internal teams should we expect to onboard to the console for runbooks/rollouts (security, platform, engineering)?

Next steps (our side):
- I'll loop in Rishi (security) and Vivek (solutions) to put together a proposed data-flow diagram and a Private VPC checklist showing how we enforce no-egress, KMS integration, and audit log retention.
- Share SOC2 + encryption details and a draft mutual action plan (MAP).

I've attached a short checklist we use for Private/VPC deployments (redwood-private-vpc-checklist.docx)  will update it with Acme-specific notes after we get your answers.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Morales <ben.morales@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Security Team <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up

Hi Marissa  thanks for the summary and for taking notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention: clinical records are retained for 7 years, yes. For audit logs related to inference activity, security policy requires retention for 5 years, with the ability to export on-demand for longer-term archives.
2) Residency: we have two larger hospitals where policy requires that data never leave our on-prem networks (no public cloud). For pilot (non-production) we can accept a US-region VPC that is logically isolated, provided there is explicit no-egress enforcement and customer-managed KMS. For production deployments at those hospitals, we will need an on-prem/air-gapped option.
3) Access: Security + Platform + DevOps will own the deployment. We'll provide a list of SAML groups that need console access.

Also attaching our compliance questionnaire and a short note from security on expected encryption standards.

Open items for Redwood to confirm:
- Can your Private deployment be configured with a zero-egress policy (network ACLs + host-level enforcement) and still support model update rollouts?
- When using customer-managed KMS, does Redwood ever store plaintext outside the KMS boundary?

Thanks  I'll await the data-flow diagram and the checklist with Acme-specific notes.

Regards,
Alice Chen
Sr. Product Security Manager | AcmeHealth
alice.chen@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme-compliance-answers.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>, Ben Morales <ben.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth - Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up

Thanks Alice  that's super helpful. Looping in Rishi (Head of Security) and Vivek (Solutions) to scope the deployment and address the on-prem constraints.

Quick answers up front so you have visibility: 
- Zero-egress: yes, we can support a zero-egress configuration for inference nodes. Our Private package can be deployed with strict network policies (no outbound NAT, host-level firewall rules, and routing that prevents egress to public IPs). Model updates can be delivered via an approved pipeline  two options: (A) customer-provided update bundle (preferred for air-gapped sites) or (B) signed model artifact push via an explicitly whitelisted management endpoint in your control plane. We'll document both patterns.
- KMS: with customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not store plaintext keys. Encryption keys remain in the KMS/HSM you control; we request access to decrypt in-memory only during runtime and do not persist plaintext key material.

Attached: acmehealth-dataflow-diagram.pdf (draft) and an updated Private VPC checklist with highlighted points for on-prem. Please review and flag anything missing.

Next steps: 
1) Alice/Ben  confirm which hospital sites require strictly on-prem.
2) Acme security  confirm retention policy for audit logs (5 years) is acceptable for our standard log pipeline; if you need longer-term cold storage, we can add export hooks.
3) Rishi/Vivek  can you put together a short runbook for model update options for air-gapped sites? Aim to have a draft by EOD Fri.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acmehealth-dataflow-diagram.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-private-vpc-checklist.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
